text.p: Actor Jimmy Stewart, who starred in such classic films as "You Can't Take It With You," "Mr. Smith Goes To Washington," and "It's A Wonderful Life," died on Wednesday, according to Daily Variety columnist Army Archerd. He was 89.
Archerd, a veteran Hollywood reporter, said Stewart died of cardiac arrest at his home in Beverly Hills. Stewart's publicist was not immediately available to comment.
Archerd said one of Stewart's children called him Wednesday morning to tell him the actor had died.
Stewart won Hollywood's biggest accolade, an Oscar, for best actor opposite Katharine Hepburn in "The Philadelphia Story" in 1940.
He gave the statuette to his father who displayed it in his hardware shop in Indiana, Pa., for 20 years.
Stewart was also nominated for five other Academy Awards.
